stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // F10 LIGHTRUNNER / SKYDIO

//Skydio

📍San Mateo, CA

Tech: Autonomous long-range flight

Platform: Fixed-wing aircraft

Goal: Give emergency responders, search teams and inspectors a live aerial view over distances measured in miles.

Why: One MegaDock could bring a rural county within reach of a single launch point, according to Skydio's figures for the F10's 30-mile flight radius.

Traction: Deploying to customers in 2027, per Skydio.

F10 is Skydio's first fixed-wing aircraft. Skydio says it can launch in seconds, fly at speeds up to 100 mph, and use a suction-based robotic gripper to launch and catch itself without a ground crew. MegaDock can house up to five F10s so a team can run concurrent missions. The company says the aircraft is designed to take off and land on its own in strong wind and to fly day or night, even in moderate rain.

Skydio also introduced Controller 2, Asset Command and Security Command, and a new Skydio Mobile App. Asset Command and Security Command are available to purchase now, with general availability early next year, and F10 deploys to customers in 2027.

Source: Skydio, Inc., September 24, 2026

Image: skydio.com (courtesy)

fields.headline: PARAVISION WINS UP TO $6.5M STATE CONTRACT
fields.deck: The award is for digital identity assurance, a category tied to deepfake and liveness tools.

stories.caption:
The U.S. State Department has awarded facial recognition developer Paravision a firm-fixed-price contract worth up to $6.5 million for "digital detection/identity assurance." The department awarded it September 23 and initially obligated $1.3 million. The contract can run through September 22, 2031.

The State Department competed the award under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and it received a single offer. Public award records do not identify which Paravision products were bought. The description overlaps with technology Paravision markets for detecting manipulated and AI-generated faces, but the record does not show whether the award includes its deepfake detection, liveness detection, facial recognition or other software.

A separate $24,717 purchase order to Paravision on April 30 was described as a "purchase card for software license." Records do not say whether that was a test, pilot or precursor to the September award.

Source: Biometric Update, 17 October 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, in the Gulf of America.

Why: Operating without a crew, the vessels can stay on station for long periods in conditions where crewed patrols are limited by endurance and cost.

Private company → Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels deployed in support of U.S. maritime border security operations, per Seasats. Earlier Lightfish vessels have operated on the Rio Grande since January 2026 under Operation River Wall.

Seasats said on Oct. 2, 2026, that a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels has been sent into the Gulf of America to support U.S. maritime border work. The company said the effort extends an autonomous surveillance program run with the Department's homeland defense office, building on its earlier work on the southern border.

Each Lightfish is about 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds. Seasats says the vessels are solar powered, can operate for multi-month periods, and can be launched by two people. Payloads reported in prior missions include electro-optical and infrared cameras, signals payloads and sonar.

Seasats describes the fleet as a way to cover offshore areas that manned aircraft and boats reach only in limited periods. Mike Flanigan, CEO of Seasats, said that a Lightfish "has no one aboard, so it can hold station for months in conditions where you wouldn't want to put a crew." The Department's Assistant Secretary of War for Homeland Defense and Americas Security Affairs, Mark R Ditlevson, said the work is part of efforts to gain full operational control of the borders.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, Oct. 2, 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

media.credit: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

MISSION BRIEF // COYOTE BLOCK 2C+RM

//Raytheon

📍Tucson, AZ

Tech: Counter-drone interceptor

Platform: Interceptor effector

Goal: Defeat current and emerging drone threats with an upgraded Coyote interceptor.

Why: A tactical rocket motor is meant to shorten engagement times and allow faster successive shots.

Ticker: NYSE: RTX

Traction: Three Raytheon-funded developmental tests completed, per Raytheon. Testing is in testing.

Raytheon says the Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrade is in developmental testing. Its first-of-its-kind launches included a Coyote effector fitted with a tactical rocket motor, and the company reports initial integration with the current counter-drone architecture. Raytheon says the effort moved from concept to testing in 15 months.

Raytheon says the upgrade builds on current Coyote variants, which have intercepted hundreds of drones in combat. The company describes a common backbone that lets the Coyote family scale across counter-drone missions.

Source: RTX, October 12, 2026

MilCityUSA ICYMI: three stories from the past week, each shown as originally published.

Microchip Technology acquired Austin-based VORAGO Technologies, adding radiation-hardened microcontrollers, microprocessors and its HARDSIL process technology to Microchip's space and defense portfolio. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Lockheed Martin unveiled PAC-3 Edge, its entry in the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor competition. The company says testing is planned for 2027, with deployment targeted by 2031.

Florida National Guard and joint partners ran Drone Crucible 26.3, an integration test at Camp Blanding from Sept. 26 to Oct. 2. The Guard said dedicated technical specialists were critical to keeping the shared operational picture working.

Source: Microchip Technology, Oct. 9, 2026; Lockheed Martin, Oct. 9, 2026; Florida National Guard report, Oct. 6, 2026.
